newsitem.title: INDIA: Thai baht float not seen hitting India rice sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht float not seen hitting India rice sales.

text.p: Thailand's currency float will make its rice exports cheaper but not affect Indian rice exports as both countries target different markets, trade officials and exporters said on Friday.
"I don't think the currency float will affect our rice exports," Anil Adlakha, executive director of the All India Rice Exporters Association (AIREA), told Reuters.
"Thailand and India have separate stratified markets," said a leading New Delhi foodgrains exporter who asked not to be identified.

Thailand on Wednesday floated the baht, dropping a 13-year-old policy of pegging it to a basket of currencies, to help bolster its sagging economy hard hit by high interest rates, low exports and high imports.

Some Indian exporters said Thai rice export prices were currently about $30 to $35 per tonne higher than all Indian grades, and if Thailand's prices fell by about $10 to $15 per tonne then they could compete with Indian rice exports.
"If the gap reduces to about $20 per tonne, then Indian rice could face competition as Thailand rice is somewhat of better quality," said Mulraj Tanna, a leading Bombay foodgrains exporter.

Export demand for Indian 100 percent broken non-Basmati rice was firming up from Nigeria and Senegal but demand for higher grades was dull as China was selling the same grades at lower prices, traders said.
"China's higher grades prices are about $20 cheaper than Indian varieties," said Prem Garg, a leading New Delhi foodgrains exporter.
Traders said Indian five percent broken non-Basmati rice was quoted at $305-$315 per tonne, FOB (free on board), 10 percent at $290-300, 15 percent at $275-285 and 25 percent at $250-260 per tonne.
They said 100 percent broken rice was quoted at $185-190 per tonne.
"The demand for 100 percent broken grades are mainly from Nigeria and Senegal," Garg said. "Shipments are continously going to them."
Tanna said there was some export demand for five percent broken grades from South Africa and Commonwealth States countries.

Adlakha said India exported 2.45 million tonnes of rice in 1996/97 (April-March) comprising two million tonnes of non-Basmati rice and 450,000 tonnes of Basmati rice. India exported 5.5 million tonnes of rice in 1995/96.
He said exports in 1997/98 were expected to be about 1.5 million to 2.0 million tonnes of non-Basmati and 400,000 to 450,000 tonnes of Basmati rice.
"But these are very preliminary figures," Adlakha said. "The target may change after monsoon report and the crop estimates."
India expects 1996/97 (July-June) rice output to be 80.54 million tonnes compared with 79.62 million in the previous year. The government has not given a rice output forecast for 1997/98.
